Likewise data/analyst-targets.json targets.TSMU is notApplicable:true — a coverage GAP, not a failed verification, so there is no external cross-check by construction. Verified close $71.5142 (data/price-quotes.json quotes.TSMU.price, verified:true, nasdaq 71.5142 / cboe 71.5142 / cnbc 71.51); derived upsideMidPct = 83/71.5142-1 = +16.06%. The pre-market print quotes.TSMU.extended.price 68.56 is verified:FALSE (nasdaq 68.56 vs cnbc 68.24 disagree) and is used for nothing. WHY THE BAND IS HELD RATHER THAN RE-CUT ON RATIO DRIFT: the band derives from TSM's FV band (valuations.TSM fvLow 390 / fvMid 487 / fvHigh 600) scaled by the TSMU/TSM price ratio, which the June entry fixed at 0.1708. It is tempting to re-scale on the current ratio and call the change decay. That is not supportable, for two reasons I verified in-repo. (1) THE RATIO IS NOT MONOTONE, so it does not measure permanent NAV decay. From single-source nasdaq raw drops: 2026-06-30 TSMU 91.72 / TSM 475.8; 2026-07-29 TSMU 54.03 / TSM 371.88; and the verified 2026-08-18 closes TSMU 71.5142 / TSM 430.97. DERIVED from those pairs, the ratio runs about 0.193, then 0.145, then 0.166 — it FELL then ROSE. Permanent decay does not mean-revert, so the ratio is dominated by a 2x fund's convexity to the underlying's level, not by drag; re-scaling off any single sample date would swing fvMid by double digits on date selection alone. (2) THE JUNE BASELINE IS NOT A CLEAN CLOSE. June's 0.1708 comes from TSMU 70.40 / TSM 412.109 in reports/raw/2026-06-05-quotes.json, runAt 2026-06-05T22:15:37Z, and reports/validation/2026-08-18-source-probe.md documents that the old adapter 'read primaryData unconditionally', i.e. a live extended-hours print rather than the official close. The June entry itself concedes the price was 'provisional, single-source (nasdaq only)'. So a small ratio delta is inside the documented session-timing error and cannot be read as structure. Moving the band on it would be exactly the drift this repo exists to prevent. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY JUSTIFY A MOVE: the band's real anchor is TSM's fundamental band, and that entry (valuations.TSM, updated 2026-06-05, nextReview 2026-07-15) is past its own review date — while TSM, unlike TSMU, HAS a verified consensus (data/analyst-targets.json targets.TSM mean 533.36, verified:true) sitting above the 487 anchor. Re-running TSM is the genuine prerequisite; until then this band is held and flagged as inheriting a stale anchor. nextReview is set to 2026-09-01 rather than ~1 month out because the June entry cites the repo's leveraged-ETF '+2주' (+14-day) review rule for this instrument.
